_readme: Level 2 Tax Code Book leaves (LevelBookLeaves). They appear after the shared book's three sections in Office_Level2 only; Level 1's book is unchanged. In Level 2 the book first opens on the first leaf below.

Sections 4-6 and 9 are reference pages for Mark the Money!, the Reviewed Schedule and the final stamp: each term is printed like the shared pages' values (readOnly: true, so it cannot be picked up) with its explanation underneath. Sections 7-8 hold the selectable finding reasons and conclusions. Headings name the place they help (blue TYPE cards, orange TREATMENT cards, Reviewed Schedule) so Arthur can send the player to a page by name.
A leaf whose body has one paragraph (blank-line separated) per value prints each paragraph under its value; keep those counts equal.
Leaves explain concepts. Never put a client's amounts, a finding, the summary answer or the stamp to choose here.

Simplified classroom rules, not legal advice. The loan-principal rule is an EDUCATIONAL DRAFT: no confirmed Philippine primary-source passage yet (see Documentation/Level2SomethingDoesNotMatch/CONTENT.md).
Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored by the game.

sections.heading: Section 4 – Income Types (Blue Cards)
sections.body:
Pay from an employer for work done as an employee. Look for a payslip and an employer.

Payment from customers for your own trade, or for a separate job you did for one. Ask: who paid, and for what work?

Payment for letting someone else use your property, such as a room or a machine.

Earnings from money or investments, such as bank interest. Check its own rule first.

Money that must be paid back. A loan release is borrowing, not earning.

sections.heading: Section 5 – Income Treatment (Orange Cards)
sections.body:
Earned income, listed with the other income of the same month. Most work and rent goes here.

Income that follows its own rule instead of the regular schedule.

Only for items a law itself excludes. Never a guess.

Money that was never earned, such as a loan that must be repaid. It stays off the schedule. An educational simplification.

sections.heading: Section 6 – Reviewed Schedule
sections.body:
A line the prepared summary already lists. Fill it with the highlighted amount from the annotated paper for the same work.

An earned payment that no summary line includes. Give it its own line, once, in its month.

Money arriving in the bank is not proof it was earned. Read why it arrived before you count it.

The one record written for that payment: the purple RECORD tag on your annotated papers.

sections.heading: Section 7 – Finding Reasons
sections.body:
A note or receipt shows money earned in the month, but no summary line and no total includes it.

Two papers give different amounts for the same thing, over the same dates.

Money arrived, but it was borrowed or must be returned, so it is not pay.

sections.heading: Section 8 – Review Conclusions
sections.body:
A record proved an earned payment was left out, and you gave it its own schedule line.

The records explain the difference: it was never earnings, or it was already counted. Nothing is added.

No record explains the difference yet. Use it only when the papers cannot settle it.

sections.heading: Section 9 – Final Assessment
sections.body:
Every earned payment has a supported line, nothing borrowed is counted, and your conclusion says what you did. Stamp READY.

Something earned is still missing, unsupported or counted twice. Fix it first, or stamp NOT READY and say why.

The Auditor reads your stamp and your handwritten summary. If the folder comes back, change only what he points to.
